title: Chat with a website
description: A multi-modal agent that can view websites, answer questions, and monitor for changes.
fulldescription: This prototype launches a multi-modal AI agent capable of 'seeing' and interacting with live websites. It uses a specialized **AWS Lambda** function running **Playwright** (a browser automation tool) to navigate to URLs and capture high-resolution screenshots. These images are processed by **Amazon Bedrock** multimodal models (like Nova or Claude), allowing you to ask questions based on the visual layout and content of the page. It also includes a 'Monitor' feature that periodically checks a website for specific visual changes and sends email alerts via **Amazon SNS**, using **Amazon DynamoDB** to track state.

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.desc: Runs the Playwright browser for screenshots and the chat logic.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.desc: Uses multimodal models to analyze the screenshots and answer queries.

services.name: Amazon API Gateway
services.desc: Exposes endpoints for the chat interface and the monitoring service.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.desc: Stores chat logs and the status of active website monitors.

services.name: S3
services.desc: Stores the captured screenshots and the frontend application.

services.name: Amazon SNS
services.desc: Sends email notifications when a monitored website changes.

💡 Cost Saving Tips
• Monitoring: Frequent polling (e.g., every minute) will increase Lambda and Bedrock costs. Use sparingly.
• Storage: Screenshots are stored in S3. Configure a lifecycle policy to delete old images if they pile up.
